target.title: fix(acp): avoid replay ledger byte scan per write
target.body:
Closes #100622

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ACP replay ledger writes repeatedly scanned the persisted replay tables to estimate serialized ledger size. On large ACP histories, each appended update could pay for a full aggregate over `acp_replay_events`, adding avoidable write-path overhead before normal retention trimming.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SQLite-backed ACP ledger now keeps a per-`DatabaseSync` ledger byte estimate cache and maintains it from the ledger's own insert/delete/update paths. The retained estimate stays scoped to ACP replay rows rather than using whole-database page counts, so the shared OpenClaw state database does not leak unrelated table size into ACP retention decisions.

This also narrows the append hot path by reading only the session row needed for `nextSeq` instead of hydrating the full replay event list before every append. Legacy file-ledger imports invalidate the estimate because they bulk-insert replay rows outside the normal append/delete helpers.

## User Impact

Users and operators with long ACP replay histories should see less write-path overhead during active ACP runs. Existing retention behavior is preserved: event-count trimming, session-count trimming, and serialized-byte trimming still mark truncated sessions incomplete.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/event-ledger.test.ts` — 14 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/translator.event-ledger.test.ts` — 3 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/event-ledger.test.ts src/acp/translator.event-ledger.test.ts` — 2 files, 17 tests passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/acp/event-ledger.ts src/acp/event-ledger.test.ts`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 src/acp/event-ledger.ts src/acp/event-ledger.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

Note: before this contributor branch existed as a PR, I used the repo's narrow local Vitest harness rather than syncing unreviewed contributor code to a credentialed Testbox. GitHub CI on the PR will provide the exact pushed-head hosted proof.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the code path and understand the change; no sanitized transcript is included in this initial PR body.
